newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia party rejects transfer of votes to rival.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia party rejects transfer of votes to rival.

text.p: The Moslem-backed United Development Party (PPP) said on Friday it would not transfer some of its votes received in last month's general elections to a rival party that gained less than the required minimum.

"We have decided not to transfer our votes to the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) and this is final. This is a consequence of the general elections... There is a winning party and there is also a losing one," PPP spokesman Usamah Hisyam told Reuters by telephone.

The Election Committee has this week lobbied the PPP, which won 23 percent of the votes in the May 29 general elections, to grant some of its votes to the PDI, which secured only three percent, down from 15 percent in the last poll in 1992.

The PDI, badly split over a leadership battle, secured only 10 seats after the elections. Under current rules, each of the three parties contesting the election must have at least one representative assigned to each of the 11 commissions that carry out the bulk of the work in the 500-seat assembly.

The idea of vote transfers came from the ruling Golkar party, which exceeded its official expectations with a sweeping 74 percent of the vote. The party has said it was willing to grant some of its votes to the PDI.
Usamah said the PPP rejected the election commission's suggestion that the transfer of votes was in the country's interest.

Provisional results of the election show that Golkar has won 325 seats in the House, the PPP 89 and the PDI 10 after the calculation of 115 million ballots. The final results will be announced on June 23.
The House of Representatives has 425 elected seats and 75 filled by the military, which does not vote.
